title: Latency-SLO Overlay and Proportional Regional Throttler for Multi-Region Routing
creator: Ava Patel
description:
Problem: During cross-region load spikes we observe wide variance in tail latency per region and cascading overload: requests bounce regions, KV cache effectiveness drops, and global SLOs slip. Current steering uses hard pins and simple hedging which results in either excessive cross-region traffic or mass shedding with poor QoE.

Goal: Introduce an SLO-aware overlay controller that modulates regional routing weight in real-time using proportional token-based throttles. The controller should: (1) Keep 95th percentile P95 latency per-region within configured SLOs while minimizing cross-region egress; (2) Coordinate with circuit breakers so regions approaching sustained overload are isolated gracefully; (3) Provide observability and knobs for rollout and emergency overrides.

This ticket is a design + implementation for the routing policy, a reference runtime shim, and integration points for Console dashboards and alerting rules.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Controller adjusts region routing weights dynamically and prevents regional P95 breaches over 5 minute windows in synthetic fault injections (bench suite).

A2: When a region's utilization crosses the defined capacity threshold, a circuit-breaker transitions through warning->partial-throttle->open states with configurable hysteresis and documented behavior.
A3: End-to-end tests demonstrate that geo pinning is honored for premium tenants while best-effort traffic is proportionally throttled back into other regions or shed according to policy.
A4: Console surfaces per-tenant/regional SLO health, current token budgets, and routing decision trace for at least 7 days of history.
A5: Rollout can be gated by feature flag and disabled via emergency kill-switch without restarting edge routers.
design_summary: Architecture: New 'SLO Overlay' component runs in the global control plane and subscribes to regional telemetry (latency histograms, queue depth, token consumption). It emits per-region weight adjustments back to the Request Director which merges them with existing routing policies (geo pin, customer preference).

Core concept: Each region maintains a token escrow that represents available serving capacity elastic to SLO headroom. Tokens are consumed per-request using a cost model (tokens per request proportional to expected token length and model context). The overlay reduces weights proportionally to token depletion rate to avoid abrupt evictions.

Circuit breaker model: Three-state CB (OK, Throttle, Open). Thresholds: Throttle at 70% of sustainable capacity, Open at 90% sustained for 2m. Hysteresis: cooldown 5m before stepping down. A degraded-routing profile limits concurrency and redirects non-pinned, low-priority traffic to fallback regions or fast-fail with 503 for critical overloads.

Latency SLOs: Default per-region SLO is P95 < 120ms for inference endpoints. SLOs are configurable per-tenant and per-route. The overlay uses smoothed P95 estimates (exp smoothing, alpha=0.2) over 1m windows to avoid oscillation.

Conflict resolution: Geo pinning takes precedence for premium routes; overlay can annotate decisions and propose degraded alternatives for pinned traffic (e.g., smaller model variant) but does not auto-rewrite pinned routes without explicit policy opt-in.
implementation_notes: Control plane: implement overlay as stateless workers with leader-election to aggregate regional metrics. Use streaming telemetry (kafka/metrics pipeline) for inputs and publish decisions to the director via the existing routing config API.

Token model: initial tokens-per-second derived from measured steady-state throughput per-region (tune during canary). Include a backpressure factor that discounts tokens based on KV cache hit degradation to avoid overloading cold caches.
Director merge logic: routing weights = base_weight * slo_overlay_factor * customer_pin_factor. Where slo_overlay_factor in [0.0,1.0] reflects safe capacity fraction.
APIs: expose /v1/overlays/{overlay_id}/status and /v1/overlays/{overlay_id}/decisions for tracing. Decisions include reason tags (latency_surge, token_exhaust, cb_open) to help Console UX.
Feature flags: implement rollout via runtime flag 'slo_overlay_v1' with per-org opt-in.
test_plan: Unit tests for token accounting, smoothing functions, and CB state transitions.
Integration tests: emulate 3-region synthetic cluster with variable latency/CPU and validate weight adjustments and final P95 behavior.
Chaos experiments: inject packet loss and CPU pressure in one region and verify graceful degradation and absence of routing loops.
Performance: ensure overlay decision path adds <2ms median latency to decision pipeline under 10k rps configuration updates.
rollout_plan: Stage 0 (internal): deploy overlay in read-only mode to gather signals for 48 hours (no decision writes).
Stage 1 (canary): enable for 5% of traffic, internal orgs only, monitor SLO delta and circuit-breaker triggers for 72h.
Stage 2 (ramped): incrementally increase to 25% then 60% traffic over 7 days if metrics stable. Adjust token cost model after canary.
Stage 3 (general): enable by default for all non-enterprise orgs; require manual opt-in for enterprise geo-pinning overrides.
Emergency rollback: kill-switch disables decision writes in <15s; Director fallback uses pre-overlay static weights.
observability_and_alerting: Dashboards: per-region SLO health, token consumption rate, CB state, routing weight deltas, and cross-region egress increases.
Alerts: P95 delta > 10% for >5m, CB opens in >1 region simultaneously, unexpected routing churn > 20% over 1m.
Audit: every decision message persisted for 14 days with routing trace id to aid incidents.
